page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance in the Eads v5 series, engineered with a constrained vCPU profile. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V on the x86_64 architecture, the instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor capable of boost frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. The hardware allocation delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical execution core via simultaneous multithreading, supported by 32 KB of L1 instruction cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside AMD SVM virtualization capabilities.

The server delivers 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage includes 161 GB of integrated local SSD storage alongside capability for external Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2696.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1583.0. In contrast, parallel throughput reflects the two-thread limit, registering a multi-core Geekbench score of 1979.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3139.36. Memory bandwidth testing shows 32.75 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 22.41 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the constrained vCPU design provides qualitative licensing efficiencies for commercial enterprise software billed on a per-core basis. By enabling 32 GB of memory on only 2 vCPUs, it circumvents higher core licensing expenses while retaining memory-tier capabilities. The inherent tradeoff is reduced raw processing power for parallel compute pipelines. Consequently, the E4-2ads_v5 is well matched for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and lightweight transactional workloads requiring large working memory sets without heavy parallel computation.
description: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with a constrained core architecture to maximize available memory per execution thread. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, accompanied by 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system RAM, yielding 16.0 GB of memory per vCPU, alongside 161 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-core compute performance with a stress-ng score of 2696.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1583.0, balanced against modest multi-core throughput due to the dual-thread ceiling. This configuration delivers licensing cost advantages for software charged per active core, making it suitable for memory-dense relational databases, enterprise transactional systems, and caching workloads requiring high RAM footprints without high CPU concurrency.
